newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-SWEDES, FRENCH IN DAVIS CUP CLIFF-HANGER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SWEDES, FRENCH IN DAVIS CUP CLIFF-HANGER.

text.p: The Davis Cup final deciding match went into a nerve-sapping fifth set on Sunday when France's Arnaud Boetsch staged a spirited comeback against Nicklas Kulti of Sweden.
Noisy spectators in the converted factory housing the tie were treated to a feast of high-tension tennis as Boetsch fought back to level the match 7-6 2-6 4-6 7-6.

Kulti pulled up with an apparently painful leg halfway through the fourth set tie-break, which Boetsch won 7-5. But the Swede continued to play, exhorting the already enthusiastic crowd to give him more support.
Earlier, top Swede Thomas Enqvist squeezed past Cedric Pioline 3-6 6-7 6-4 6-4 9-7 in a gripping four-and-a half hour duel.
"That was the longest match of my career and probably the most emotional," Enqvist said afterwards.
Kulti replaced veteran campaigner Stefan Edberg who pulled out of the last match of his professional career after twisting his ankle in the opening singles on Friday.
